clue.text: Challenge over part of form I release to public

indicators.note: the challenge word sits over, covering, the other pieces, so it wraps around them

parts.note: to challenge someone is to defy them
a school form is divided into classes, so a class is part of one
the letter I taken straight from the clue

explanation.surface: Someone filling in a form decides to publish what they have written.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a year group or class; the setter treats a class as a piece of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To declassify secret documents is to make them available to the public.

clue.text: Part of Ireland (see above)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: County ... in Northern Ireland
second meaning: the heading printed above this clue in the list, the direction of the clue itself

explanation.walkthrough: This is 1 down, so the heading above it in the clue list is the answer itself; County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an Irish county and also the heading over the clue list for vertical entries.

clue.text: Travellers in company in vehicles going round area

indicators.note: the two vehicles go round, surrounding, the letter for area

parts.note: two vehicles side by side, a car and a van

explanation.surface: People travelling together in a convoy of vehicles drive round a region.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a group of travellers journeying together, such as merchants crossing a desert.

clue.text: Go from nine to five with 50 per cent less effort thus?

definitions.text: Go from nine to five with 50 per cent less effort thus?

parts.note: reads as working office hours, but means moving a clock hand from the 9 to the 5

parts.words: with 50 per cent less effort thus?
parts.note: going the short way round the dial covers four hours instead of eight, half the distance

explanation.walkthrough: Nine to five suggests a working day; on a clock face, turning the hand backwards from 9 to 5 is four hours, half the eight needed going forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving against the normal direction of clock hands is the short route from the nine to the five.

clue.text: Eastern European holding up what's exemplary

indicators.note: the national holds, contains, the word up within it

parts.note: a Serb is a native of Serbia in eastern Europe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person from Eastern Europe is held up as a model of excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superb is outstanding, the kind of excellent thing held up as a model.

clue.text: Understood grief at home defeat to some extent

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, so the answer lies within it

parts.note: the answer runs across these words, from the end of grief to the start of defeat

explanation.surface: A fan grasped the sadness of losing a home match.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fathomed something is to have got to the bottom of it, grasping its meaning.

clue.text: Gang was audibly triumphant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a team or band of workers
second meaning: an old past tense of crow, to boast loudly in triumph

explanation.walkthrough: Besides crowed, the past tense of crow can be this older form, as in 'the cock crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a working team, and it is also an archaic past tense of the verb meaning to exult.

clue.text: Pay more attention, as doctor, to back

definitions.text: Pay more attention, as doctor, to
definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., to give a patient further treatment
second meaning: to back away, withdraw

explanation.walkthrough: Split as re-treat it is a doctor's second go; as one word it is a withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the word means to withdraw or move backwards, and split it means to give medical care again.

clue.text: Extra small page perused, in general

parts.note: a wide is a cricket extra, a run given for a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach
perused means read through, past tense

explanation.surface: A tiny extra page has been read, in a broad sense.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is one of the extras, runs not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread is general, found over a large area or among many people.

clue.text: Secretly listen to Western pirate broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eavesdropping on an illegal Western radio station's transmissions.
explanation.definitionFit: To wiretap is to tap a telephone line so as to eavesdrop on calls.

clue.text: Hero of Dickens novel editor distorted

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the title hero of Dickens's novel

explanation.surface: An editor has mangled the protagonist of a Dickens book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something twisted is bent out of shape, warped from its true form.

clue.text: One pair of partners — religious, intelligent, and uplifting

parts.note: in bridge North and South play as partners
pi is informal for pious, religious
rational means able to reason, sensible

explanation.surface: A couple who are devout and clever are a source of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is played by two partnerships, North-South and East-West, so N and S make a pair of partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inspirational lifts the spirits and motivates, as an uplifting speech does.

clue.text: Savagery around a king that's not personally experienced

indicators.note: the savagery word goes around the other two pieces

parts.note: viciousness is fierce brutality
taken as written

explanation.surface: Brutality surrounds a monarch, though he only hears of it at second hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicariousness is the quality of something felt through another person rather than lived oneself.

clue.text: These sources of rumours enrage VIPs misrepresented

indicators.note: presented in a false shape, so these letters are set out in another order

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words are the raw material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Gossip networks infuriate celebrities by telling lies about them.
explanation.walkthrough: To hear something on the grapevine is to hear it as rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapevine is the informal chain of gossip by which rumours spread.

clue.text: Managed to complete minutes in no particular order

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: Someone got through the meeting's minutes, though in a jumbled way.
explanation.definitionFit: Random arrangement follows no pattern or plan, which is the same as having no set sequence.

clue.text: Go-between one somehow has to admire

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged in an unspecified new order

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words are the raw material to rearrange

explanation.surface: An intermediary must find some way to admire the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator is an intermediary who carries proposals between two parties in a dispute.

clue.text: Relating to community in that way, clubs I and others joined

parts.note: so means thus, in that manner
the letter I taken straight from the clue
et al. is Latin shorthand for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Membership societies and individuals have all signed up together.
explanation.definitionFit: Societal describes things belonging to society, the whole community of people.

clue.text: Marine organisms not turned over on board

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed on, after, the board in the answer

parts.note: a plank is a long board of timber

indicators.note: the word not is flipped so it reads backwards

parts.note: the word not taken as written, before being flipped

explanation.surface: Sea creatures that do not capsize when aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the tiny drifting animals and plants that live in seas and lakes.

clue.text: Spraying can damage a rose — nothing left

indicators.note: the words a rose are damaged, knocked into a different arrangement

parts.note: the five letters of these words are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A garden spray might harm a rose, leaving it with no blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb, as in being able to damage, but it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised canister that releases its contents as a fine spray.

clue.text: Unknown leading African country replaced by good leader in this one

indicators.note: the unknown letter stands at the front of the country's name
the letter at the front is swapped out for the new initial

parts.note: Zambia is a country in southern Africa
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the word good is used

parts.note: the word good supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: An African nation's leadership, once unknown, was taken over by a good leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing the first letter of one African country gives another, and 'this one' points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is itself a West African state, the 'one' referred to by the clue.

clue.text: Being inclined to disallow ruler's financial activity?

definitions.meaning: banking is tilting, as an aircraft does in a turn
a noun phrase standing for the business of banks

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
a king is a ruler of a kingdom

explanation.surface: A monarch is minded to forbid money dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions surround the wordplay: an aircraft banks by tilting, and banking is the work of banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Banking is both tilting at an angle in a turn and the business of handling money.

clue.text: Old man's covering miles in vast plains

indicators.note: the father's word covers, wraps round, the abbreviation for miles

parts.note: an old man is a father, papa, and the 's adds the S

explanation.surface: A father's property spreads over miles of open grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: The pampas are the grassy lowlands of Argentina and Uruguay.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are huge treeless grasslands of South America.

clue.text: Check about second work of poet

indicators.note: the check word goes about, around, the letter for second

parts.note: verification is checking that something is true

explanation.surface: A second look at a poet's next poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal for the work, but it is the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: Versification is the craft of composing verse, which is what a poet does.

clue.text: Recited pieces of poetry, quite an achievement

indicators.note: recited means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: metrical feet are the units of a line of verse

explanation.surface: Reciting verse from memory is a real accomplishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable deed requiring skill or courage.

clue.text: Backed an aromatic product that's just coming out

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the little word is read the other way

parts.note: the word an taken as written, before being flipped
a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: Someone invested in a perfume about to be launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' reads as financed, but it signals reading the word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, emerging.

clue.text: Thoughtful writers I have abridged

parts.note: pens are writing implements
the letter I taken straight from the clue

indicators.note: have is cut short, as in the contraction I've

parts.note: the word have taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Reflective authors confess to having trimmed their work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensive describes someone deep in thought, reflective.

clue.text: Not quite as depressed, how one can perform

indicators.note: the phrase is not quite complete, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: so low means as depressed, that downcast

explanation.surface: A performer who is not feeling so down any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo means alone, the way a single performer plays without others.

clue.text: Source of illumination to secure inside staircase

indicators.note: the securing word goes inside the staircase word

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs
to lash is to tie securely

explanation.surface: A lamp is fixed to the inside of a stairwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashlight is a torch, a portable electric lamp.
